subject: hep-th
title_original: Self-dual holography: four-point AdS/CFT correlators in higher-spin gravity
abstract: Self-dual theories, being UV-finite, should have their own AdS/CFT dualities. Higher-spin extensions of self-dual theories are attractive to simplify the CFT duals. The maximal self-dual theory is Chiral higher-spin gravity, which should be dual to a subsector of Chern--Simons matter theories. As a step toward establishing self-dual holography, we develop the Fefferman--Graham expansion and holographic dictionary for arbitrary spin self-dual theories. As an application, we derive bulk-to-bulk propagators and compute three- and four-point AdS/CFT correlators in a contraction of Chiral higher-spin gravity, which is a higher-spin extension of self-dual Yang--Mills theory.
title_relatable: Can simplified gravity theories unlock hidden AdS/CFT duals?
hook: Self-dual gravity theories eliminate infinities. Physicists map their four-point correlators using higher-spin extensions, testing whether simpler theories have their own holographic mirrors.
summary: Self-dual theories don't blow up at high energies, suggesting they deserve their own AdS/CFT dictionary—the physicist's Rosetta Stone linking bulk gravity to boundary quantum fields. The authors develop the mathematical tools (Fefferman–Graham expansion) to translate between sides and compute four-point correlators in a higher-spin version of self-dual Yang–Mills theory, a simplified test case that could unlock new holographic dualities.
